title: Dimension at a point of a finite type affine scheme from its irreducible components
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x\in X$ correspond to a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset S$. Then the Krull dimension of $X$ at $x$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals the maximum of the Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (with the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]) of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ which contain $x$. Equivalently, if $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ are the minimal prime ideals of $S$ (prime ideals containing no strictly smaller prime ideal) contained in $\mathfrak p$, then $t\ge1$ and $$\dim_xX=\max_{1\le i\le t}\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i),$$ where the right hand side uses ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; this is a non-negative integer. It also equals the minimum of $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ over the maximal ideals $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and this minimum is attained.

proof.text: Construct qs as the finite set of minimal primes below p using Noetherianity of the finite type algebra. A minimal prime exists below p. Every quotient S/q in qs is a finite type domain. The finite-type-domain dimension theorem supplies its uniquely determined finite natural dimension; choose its numerical representation and take an attained maximum n using Finset.exists_max_image.

proof.text: Identify irreducible components with zero loci of minimal primes. The closed embedding Spec(S/q) into Spec S induces a homeomorphism onto V(q). Homeomorphism invariance and the spectrum/ring dimension equality give dim V(q) = dim S/q. The maximum and its attainment therefore give both component clauses.

proof.text: For a prime q below a maximal m, map m to a maximal ideal M of S/q. The finite-type-domain theorem identifies dim S/q with dim (S/q)_M. Strict monotonicity of prime comap for the surjective quotient map bounds height M by height m. Localization dimension is prime height, giving dim S/q <= dim S_m. Apply this to the quotient attaining n to prove the lower bound for every maximal m above p.

proof.text: Every open neighbourhood W of p contains a basic open D(f) through p. The Jacobson equality p.jacobson = p gives a maximal ideal m above p excluding f, hence a maximal ideal in W.

proof.text: For any prime m in an open W, dim S_m <= dim W. The ambient height of m equals the coheight of its irreducible closure through the order isomorphism between primes and irreducible closed sets. The open-subspace map preserves this coheight, and coheight is at most the Krull dimension of W. This proves the neighbourhood lower bound n <= dim W using the maximal ideal from the previous step.

proof.text: Remove the finite union T of V(q) over minimal primes q not below p, obtaining an open neighbourhood U. Map any strict chain c of irreducible closed subsets of U to its closures in Spec S and then, in reversed order, to prime ideals. Take a minimal prime q below the smallest prime in this reversed chain. The largest closed subset c.last has a point y in U; its closure lies in V(q), so q cannot be among the removed primes. Thus q belongs to qs. All primes of the chain contain q. Restricting the prime chain to V(q) preserves its length, which is at most dim S/q <= n. Taking the supremum of chain lengths gives dim U <= n.

proof.text: The infimum defining dim_p Spec S is at least n by the neighbourhood lower bound and at most n using U. A maximal m above p in U has n <= dim S_m <= dim U <= n, so its localization has dimension exactly n and realizes the required minimum. Assemble this with qs, the attained quotient maximum and the component clauses.

lean.statement: theorem dimension_at_point_components {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] : let X := Spec (CommRingCat.of S) let x : X := ⟨p, inferInstance⟩ ∃ qs : Finset (Ideal S), (∀ q : Ideal S, q ∈ qs ↔ q.IsPrime ∧ q ≤ p ∧ ∀ r : Ideal S, r.IsPrime → r ≤ q → r = q) ∧ qs.Nonempty ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDimAt x = n ∧ (∀ Z : Set X, Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X → x ∈ Z → topologicalKrullDim Z ≤ n) ∧ (∃ Z : Set X, Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X ∧ x ∈ Z ∧ topologicalKrullDim Z = n) ∧ (∀ q ∈ qs, ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) ≤ n) ∧ (∃ q ∈ qs, ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) = n) ∧ (∀ (m : Ideal S) [m.IsMaximal], p ≤ m → (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime m)) ∧ (∃ (m : Ideal S) (_ : m.IsMaximal), p ≤ m ∧ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime m) = n)
